states.description: A candidate concern exists outside the executable queue.
The package is queueable and has declared lane, owner, boundary, scope, and proof.
The package owns the current execution slice and current-blocker projection.
The package closed atomically with evidence, validation, package rename, and sprint/current-blocker refresh.
The package is no longer executable because a successor, migration, or architecture decision replaced it.

transitions.evidence: npm run work:package:new -- --write with lane, owner, boundary, dominant reason, scope, and proof.
npm run work:sprint:queue -- --activate refreshes current-blocker and active sprint references.
npm run work:close runs repair, closure validation, package rename, current-blocker refresh, focused staging, and close commit.
The active package records successor or migration evidence before package status changes.
The todo package records why a newer route, owner, or architecture decision replaced it.

forbiddenTransitions.reason: Closed package evidence is immutable; new work needs a successor package.
Superseded packages cannot silently become the active owner of a later route.
Closure requires validation, execution evidence, and package/sprint/current-blocker atomicity.

invariants.statement: An active package must name exactly one owner and boundary as the executable slice.
A package cannot enter done without replayable closure evidence and workflow repair.
A superseded package records the successor, migration, or architecture decision that replaced it.
